issues.legal_issue: Compulsory deprivation of private property by the State without legal authority or due process requires compensation.
material_facts: The State took the owner’s land for construction of a public road without initiating acquisition proceedings or following another legally prescribed process.
The State admitted that it had used the land and had not initiated acquisition proceedings for it.
The owner had received no compensation for the taking.
issues.conclusion: The taking without legal sanction or due process violated the owner’s right to property, and the State was directed to pay compensation.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31, applicable when the land was taken, protected property from deprivation without due process and just and fair compensation. After the Forty-Fourth Amendment, the right to property remained a constitutional right under Article 300A and a human right; deprivation must be authorized by law, and an obligation to compensate can be inferred from Article 300A. The Court relied on The State of West Bengal v. Subodh Gopal Bose, Tukaram Kana Joshi v. M.I.D.C., K.T. Plantation Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Karnataka, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd. v. Darius Shapur Chenai, N. Padmamma v. S. Ramakrishna Reddy, Delhi Airtech Services Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P., and Jilubhai Nanbhai Khachar v. State of Gujarat.

rule.if: state_compulsory_taking_case and state_took_private_property and no_legal_process_followed and no_compensation_paid

predicates.state_compulsory_taking_case: The proceeding concerns the State’s compulsory taking of private property.
predicates.state_took_private_property: The State took or used a person’s private property for a public purpose.
predicates.no_legal_process_followed: The State did not follow a legally authorized process to take the property.
predicates.no_compensation_paid: The owner received no compensation for the taking.

issues.definition: When the State takes private property for a public purpose without a legally authorized process and pays no compensation, it must compensate the owner for the unlawful taking.

issues.legal_issue: The State cannot acquire title to a citizen’s property by relying on adverse possession when its possession began with an unlawful taking.
material_facts: The State had remained in possession of the land since taking it for road construction without legal sanction.
The State argued that its long possession had converted its title into adverse possession.
issues.conclusion: The State could not rely on adverse possession to perfect title over the citizen’s land.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that a welfare State cannot invoke adverse possession to grab a citizen’s property after taking it without legal sanction. It referred to State of Haryana v. Mukesh Kumar and the principle discussed in Tukaram Kana Joshi v. M.I.D.C. that the State must use a lawful procedure to acquire or requisition property.

predicates.government_adverse_possession_claim: The government claims that its possession has given it title by adverse possession.
predicates.government_possession_began_with_unlawfu: The government’s possession began when it took a citizen’s property without legal sanction.

issues.definition: If the government claims adverse possession over property it first possessed through an unlawful taking, it cannot perfect title by adverse possession.

issues.legal_issue: Delay and laches do not bar constitutional relief where an unlawful deprivation of property is continuing and the demand for justice is compelling.
material_facts: The owner was an illiterate rural widow who had not sought relief for many years after the State took her land.
The State had admitted that it took the land without acquisition proceedings or another process known to law.
The owner remained uncompensated, and the Court treated the cause of action as continuing.
The High Court had declined to determine the claim in writ proceedings on the basis of disputed questions and delay.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the State’s delay-and-laches objection and exercised its extraordinary jurisdiction to grant relief.
issues.legal_principle: Delay and laches do not necessarily bar relief for a continuing cause of action or where the circumstances shock the judicial conscience. Whether delay should be condoned depends on the circumstances, including the breach of fundamental rights, the remedy sought, and the reason for the delay; there is no prescribed limitation period for constitutional courts exercising their jurisdiction to do substantial justice. The Court relied on Tukaram Kana Joshi v. M.I.D.C. and referred to P.S. Sadasivaswamy v. State of T.N.

predicates.constitutional_relief_proceeding: The claimant seeks relief in a constitutional proceeding concerning deprivation of property.
predicates.continuing_unlawful_property_deprivation: The claimant remains deprived of property taken without legal sanction and has not received compensation.
predicates.compelling_demand_for_justice: The circumstances make the demand for judicial relief compelling.

issues.definition: In a constitutional relief proceeding, delay does not bar relief when unlawful property deprivation continues and the circumstances make the demand for justice compelling.

issues.legal_issue: Compensation for an unlawful taking may be assessed by reference to the award for similarly situated land acquired for the same purpose, with applicable statutory benefits.
material_facts: The State had taken the owner’s land for the same public purpose and at the same time as neighbouring land.
A court had directed acquisition of the neighbouring owners’ land, and a Reference Court had later awarded compensation for it.
The owner’s land had not been included in those acquisition proceedings despite being similarly situated.
issues.conclusion: The State was directed to pay compensation on the same terms as the Reference Court’s award for the neighbouring land, with statutory benefits, treating the case as a deemed acquisition.
issues.legal_principle: In exercising its jurisdiction under Articles 136 and 142, the Court treated the case as one of deemed acquisition and used the Reference Court’s award for similarly situated land as the compensation benchmark, including statutory benefits under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

predicates.court_ordered_compensation_case: The court is determining compensation for property taken by the State without a completed acquisition process.
predicates.land_taken_for_same_purpose_as_comparabl: The claimant’s land and comparable land were taken for the same public purpose.
predicates.comparable_land_has_court_award: A court has awarded compensation for the comparable land.

issues.definition: Where compensation is being ordered for an unlawful taking and comparable land taken for the same purpose has a court award, compensation may follow that award with applicable statutory benefits.

issues.legal_issue: A later appeal concerning the compensation award is to be treated as within limitation if filed within the court-fixed window after compensation is paid.
material_facts: The Court directed the State to pay compensation to the owner.
The Court provided that an appeal could be filed after payment and would be treated as within limitation if filed within the specified window.
issues.conclusion: An appeal filed within the court-fixed window after compensation is paid must be treated as within limitation and decided on its merits in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: The Court made a specific procedural direction in exercising its jurisdiction under Articles 136 and 142, allowing a later compensation appeal to be treated as within limitation if filed within the stipulated period after payment.

predicates.compensation_ordered_by_court: The court has ordered payment of compensation for the property taken.
predicates.appeal_concerns_compensation_determinati: The claimant seeks to appeal a determination concerning compensation for the taken property.
predicates.appeal_filed_within_court_fixed_window_a: The claimant files the appeal within the window set by the court after compensation is paid.

issues.definition: If a court has ordered compensation and the related compensation appeal is filed within the court-fixed window after payment, the appeal is treated as within limitation.
